summary: In the temple, the chief priests, scribes and elders demand to know by what authority Jesus acts. He asks them about John’s baptism, and they refuse to answer.
key_insight: The leaders never asked each other whether John was sent by God. They asked only which answer was safe: “If we say…” Their “We do not know” was not ignorance but a refusal. Jesus would not hand His credentials to men who had already decided what to do with the truth.
story: Jesus and His disciples came again to Jerusalem. {Mk} One of those days, as He was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the gospel, {Lk} the chief priests, the scribes and the elders came to Him as He walked in the temple courts. {Mk}
“By what authority are You doing these things?” they demanded. “And who gave You this authority to do these things?” {Mk}

Jesus answered, “I also will ask you one question; then answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.” He asked them about the baptism of John: “was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me.” {Mk}

They reasoned among themselves: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.” {Lk}
So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
differences: Luke alone says Jesus was teaching the people and preaching the gospel when the leaders came.
Matthew names the chief priests and the elders; Mark and Luke add the scribes.
The leaders’ fear is told in different words: “we fear the multitude” (Matthew), they “feared the people” (Mark), “all the people will stone us” (Luke).
In Mark and Luke Jesus tells them, “answer Me”; Mark has Him say it twice.

scene.label: An official delegation
scene.text: Chief priests, scribes and elders were the three groups that made up the Sanhedrin, the ruling council (compare Mark 15:1). This was not a passing question from the crowd. The council’s leaders came to call Jesus to account in their own temple.

scene.label: “These things”
scene.text: The leaders meant all that Jesus had done since Sunday: the royal entry, the clearing of the market, healings and teaching in courts the priests controlled. Only the priests had authority over the temple, and Jesus held no office or title from them.

scene.label: A teacher without credentials
scene.text: Teachers in Israel usually taught by citing the rabbis before them. Jesus had studied under none of them. Months earlier, people had asked, “How does this Man know letters, having never studied?” (John 7:15).

scene.label: John’s baptism
scene.text: John had baptized crowds from Jerusalem and all Judea (Mark 1:5), and he had pointed to Jesus as the One coming after him (John 1:26–34). To say John was from heaven was to accept his witness about Jesus. That is why the question answered theirs.

witnesses.matthew: Uses this exchange to open three parables aimed at the leaders (21:28–22:14). The next words in Matthew turn John’s ministry against them: tax collectors and harlots believed John, and the leaders did not.
witnesses.mark: Has Jesus press them twice, “answer Me,” and breaks off the leaders’ reasoning in mid-sentence before explaining that they feared the people. The broken sentence sounds like speech remembered.
witnesses.luke: Sets the challenge on one of the days Jesus was teaching and “preached the gospel” in the temple, and records the leaders’ blunt fear that the people would stone them. In Luke the people’s eagerness to hear Jesus is what holds the leaders back (19:48; 20:19).

seeing.reveals: Jesus’ authority does not come from any council. He needs no permission to cleanse His Father’s house, and He will not put His credentials before men who had already rejected God’s messenger.
seeing.living: The leaders’ question sounded honest, but their hearts were made up. They had decided about John long before; they simply would not say it. When Jesus’ claims press on you, do not say “I do not know” when the truth is “I will not.” He answers honest seekers; He does not perform for people who have already decided.
seeing.ponder: Is there something about Jesus you avoid saying out loud because of what it would cost you?

preaching.big_idea: Those who refuse the light God has given cannot demand more.
outline: A question that exposes the heart (29–30)
preaching.watch_for: The leaders reason only about consequences: what Jesus will say and what the people will do (vv. 31–32). Whether John spoke the truth never enters their discussion. Their “We do not know” (v. 33) is the answer of men protecting their position.
